text:
maria_ng: Heads-up — DAST job `nightly-staging-dast` started failing around 03:10 UTC with a 403 on the test-login flow. This started after the RBAC cleanup that removed some old service roles.

josh_leung: ugh, saw alerts. Error in CI logs shows KMS decrypt failure for the scanner creds too. Full snippet below. Not sure if it's RBAC or keystore rotation.

kevin_smith: paste the snippet?

josh_leung: ```
ERROR: failed to fetch secrets: kms.Decrypt RPC error: permission denied: projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/keystore/cryptoKeys/scanner-key: caller does not have permission
DAST: auth handshake failed with staging SSO (403)
```

maria_ng: @tamara_oncall can you check if the keystore IAM change landed in the deploy window last night? I think the scanner service account lost cryptoKeyDecrypter role.

tamara_oncall: looking now. I see a policy diff in the audit log: `removed roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter from serviceAccount:scanner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` by infra-bot at 02:47 UTC. It references a cleanup PR from infra-team.

oliver_dev: that matches. Infra ran a least-privilege pass. They missed the scanner principal. We should treat as incident (impacting security testing).

maria_ng: Agreed. Quick triage steps: 1) add scanner SA back to cryptoKeyDecrypter on the specific key as emergency temporary fix; 2) re-run DAST canary; 3) capture audit entries and assign owner for permanent policy update/review; 4) ensure we record for postmortem.

sec-bot: Incident created: SECINC-2026-014. Owner assigned: tamara_oncall. SLA: high (DAST coverage lost).

tamara_oncall: I can re-grant temporarily and run canary now. Will also pin audit evidence.

kevin_smith: If we re-grant, please scope the grant to the single cryptoKey resource instead of whole keyring. Also consider short-lived grant with expiration tag.

tamara_oncall: done — granted `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` on resource `projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/keystore/cryptoKeys/scanner-key` to scanner SA, expiration 4 hours. Reran DAST job; initial stages passed, full suite running.

maria_ng: Nice. Two follow-ups: 1) infra needs to update their cleanup playbook to exclude scanner principal (or have an allowlist) — open a PR referencing SECINC-2026-014; 2) update our SDLC gating to flag when scanner auth errors surface (fail-gate with a specific alert).

josh_leung: For the PR, suggest adding a validation check in the infra cleanup job: query recent CI/runbook ownership for service accounts used by scanning tools and skip them. I can draft the change.

oliver_dev: Also add an automated smoke-run after any key or IAM change that touches keystore to detect breakage early. Could run a minimal auth check with the scanner SA via signed JWT exchange.

maria_ng: Good idea. For the postmortem, capture: timeline of RBAC change, who approved PR, which tests failed and when, audit log excerpts, mitigation steps, and long-term mitigation (allowlist + smoke-run + infra PR). Assign to kevin_smith + infra lead.

tamara_oncall: I've attached audit log link in the incident ticket and put a temporary annotation in the DAST pipeline to skip flaky runs while we stabilize.

kevin_smith: One more action: update SAST/DAST runbook to include KMS permission checks as part of preflight for nightly runs. Snippet for preflight check:

```bash
# preflight: ensure scanner can decrypt test token
gcloud kms decrypt 
  --ciphertext-file=/tmp/ct 
  --location=global 
  --keyring=keystore 
  --key=scanner-key 
  --project=redwood-prod \ 
  --impersonate-service-account=scanner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com || exit 1
```

maria_ng: Love it. After the incident: 1) permanent IAM change reviewed in infra PR with exceptions list, 2) add smoke-run + preflight to pipelines, 3) update runbook and have oncall practice once.

tamara_oncall: marking incident as mitigated — DAST full suite completed successfully at 04:12 UTC. Will leave SECINC-2026-014 open for postmortem ops.

josh_leung: Thanks folks. Quick note: audit logs show the removal was automated via `infra-cleaner` job which used a stale allowlist. I'll follow up with infra to add stricter tests.

oliver_dev: Recommend adding a CI gating test for infra-cleaner PRs: run a job that simulates removing roles and verifies no critical SAs (scanner, buildbot, deployer) lose needed perms.

maria_ng: Ok team — next steps captured in ticket. If anyone wants to take postmortem writeup, volunteer now — else I'll draft.

kevin_smith: I'll co-author with maria.

maria_ng: thanks. Closing discussion here — please add notes to SECINC-2026-014. :thumbsup:
